name: bitblocks-election-count-vectors
description: Test vectors for the counting rule of an open-ballot election recorded on BSV: who may vote, which ballots count, the tally and the winners. Each vector gives the input and the outcome to match, so anyone can recount an election archive with their own code and check it against ours.
claim: These vectors cover the count only. They take as given that each ballot's signer is the address whose AIP signature checked; that the signature covers every MAP field of its record, since an AIP over chosen field indexes that leaves a MAP field out counts for nothing (as for BAP); that roll.members are the members in the roll file at election.roll, whose exact bytes hash to election.roll_sha256; and that each height is on the chain the headers agree on. Checking signatures, tx bytes, the roll file, merkle proofs and headers comes before the count.
draft_fields: The record field names follow Open Civic Data and NIST SP 1500-100 where they overlap (name, number_elected, votes_allowed). They, the vector ids and the outcomes here may still change in v0, until the first election record is published on chain.
versioning: v0 is a draft: nothing consumes it yet, and a vector may change. Once the first election record is published, a v1 file freezes the inputs: within v1 a vector's id, input and expected outcome stay as they are, except to correct a mistake; new vectors raise the minor version; and a change to the rule gets a new file.
how_to_use: For each vector, run your counter on input.election, input.roll and input.ballots, with input.close_block_hash when it is present.
Compare your answer with expected. Ballots are listed in chain order: by height, then position, with unconfirmed ballots last by txid.
A ballot is listed against the first rule it fails, in rule_order. Only a ballot that passes every rule before replaced can replace another.
Where expected has error, a counter refuses the whole input. error_detail is the wording Bitblocks uses, so yours may differ.
Signers, txids and candidate ids are compared as exact strings. In real records a signer is a P2PKH address and a txid is 64 hex characters; the vectors use short signers to stay readable.

records.encoding: Each record is a MAP SET signed with AIP over every MAP field. A list (choices, candidates) is one JSON array in a single MAP value, since a repeated MAP key keeps only its last value. An integer (number_elected, votes_allowed, a height) is decimal ASCII with no leading zeros.
records.ids: An election is named by its record's outpoint, <txid>.<vout>, the txid as lowercase hex in display order. Ballots and the result name that outpoint in election.
records.roll: Published first, as a JSON B:// file {"members": [...]}, sorted and unique, naming no election. The election record names it by outpoint in roll, with roll_sha256 over its exact bytes on chain. Both must confirm below opens_at_height.

fields.election: The election record: election (its outpoint), name, number_elected (how many win), votes_allowed (how many a ballot may name; defaults to number_elected), candidates (each id, of a-z, 0-9 and -, and name), the window opens_at_height to closes_at_height (both ends included), roll (the roll file's outpoint), roll_sha256, and height (the block it confirmed in, below opens_at_height; optional).
fields.roll: members: the P2PKH addresses allowed to vote, exactly as the AIP signature writes them, sorted by UTF-8 bytes and each once. A compressed and an uncompressed key give different addresses, so the roll lists the one the member's wallet signs with. height: the block the roll confirmed in, below opens_at_height (optional).
fields.ballot: txid; election (the outpoint it names); height (null while unconfirmed or after a reorg removed its block); position (the tx's index in its block, coinbase 0, the same as its BUMP leaf offset); signer (the address whose AIP signature checked, or null); choices (candidate ids).
fields.close_block_hash: The hash of the block at closes_at_height, as lowercase hex in RPC and display order (as getblockhash and explorers show it), the reverse of the header's internal byte order. Known only after close, it settles a tie for the last seats.
fields.expected.ballots: Each ballot's txid, counted, rule (the first rule it failed, or null) and replaced_by (the txid that replaced it, or null).
fields.expected.tally: Votes per candidate, in the election's order, zeros included. A ballot gives one vote to each candidate it names.
fields.expected.winners: Candidates with at least one vote, most votes first, up to number_elected. Candidates tied above the boundary all win, in the election's order. A tie for the last seats goes by lot (see tie_rule), listed in lot order.
fields.expected.undecided: null, or the seats still open and the tied candidates for them, when a tie for the last seats has no close_block_hash to settle it.

rules.no_signature: No AIP signature checked (signer is null).
rules.unconfirmed: It isn't in a block (height is null).
rules.malformed_choices: choices isn't a list of strings.
rules.too_many_choices: It names more than votes_allowed candidates.
rules.unknown_candidate: It names an id not in candidates.
rules.replaced: The same signer has a later ballot, in chain order, that passed every rule before this one; replaced_by is its txid.

tie_rule: When candidates tie for the last seats, order them by sha256 of the UTF-8 string "<close_block_hash>:<candidate id>", as lowercase hex, lowest first, and fill the seats left. close_block_hash is lowercase hex in RPC and display order, the reverse of the header's internal byte order. The block at closes_at_height isn't known while voting is open, so no one can steer the lot, and anyone can check it from the headers.

vectors.description: Four members vote inside the window. Every ballot counts; Ada and Ben take the two seats.
The window includes both ends: a ballot at opens_at_height and one at closes_at_height count, one a block before or after doesn't.
A ballot signed by a key that isn't on the roll is listed and not counted.
A ballot whose AIP signature didn't check has signer null and doesn't count.
A ballot for another election is listed against the rule it fails first, and not counted.
A ballot not yet in a block (height null), or whose block a reorg removed, waits: it doesn't count until it confirms.

With two to elect and votes_allowed left to default to number_elected: three names is too many, one name twice is a duplicate, an id not on the list is unknown, and a string where a list belongs is malformed. None of them counts.
A member votes twice. The later one in chain order counts, and the earlier one is replaced by it.
Two ballots from one member in the same block: the higher position (the tx's index in the block) is later and counts. Input order doesn't matter; the ballots are given here in reverse.
A later ballot that fails a rule (here an unknown candidate, and one after close) doesn't replace the member's earlier counted ballot.
An empty ballot is valid and votes for no one, so a later empty ballot withdraws the member's earlier votes.
Ada and Ben tie for first with two seats to fill. Both win, listed in the election's order; no lot is needed.
Ada leads; Ben, Cy and Di tie for the last seat. Without close_block_hash (voting still open) that seat is undecided.

The same ballots, with the hash of the block at closes_at_height. Each tied candidate's lot is sha256 of "<close_block_hash>:<id>" as lowercase hex: ben cdb52145fbc5619e76482acef5bdcd3306932587ba8b9a287b5b7a62417a1ebe, cy 2f609dcdfe47fafe4383bfbb445a5e0075adafa2d44ec953a402c0d1455141a6, di ca5e18ad2c5c8d844210c10363f960bae6a19f5a718eb7fab7d47dfcec6cdfa3. The lowest, cy, takes the seat.
A candidate needs at least one vote to win, so with three seats and two candidates voted for, one seat stays empty.
A ballot that fails several rules is listed against the first, in rule_order: here an outsider's late ballot with too many names is not_on_roll.
One to elect, and each ballot may name up to two (votes_allowed 2). Two names count; three is too many. Ada has two votes to Ben's one and takes the seat.
The election must be a map (a JSON object).
